sections.h2: Where is the Currituck County Register of Deeds, and what is its job?
sections.html:
The Currituck County Register of Deeds is at 153 Courthouse Road, Suite 600, in the community of Currituck, NC 27929, and the footer of the county's fee page lists weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The office records, indexes and preserves real estate and business documents, issues marriage licenses and certified birth and death records, and provides certified copies of anything on record for a fee.

Staff show visitors how to search the records, but the office states it cannot give legal advice, prepare documents or run a title search. Beach properties in Corolla and mainland properties near Moyock and Knotts Island are all recorded through this one office, since it keeps the records for the whole county.

sections.h2: What two transfer taxes apply to a Currituck County sale?
sections.html:
The county's fee page shows two separate levies on a real estate conveyance. One is the state excise stamp tax, $1.00 for each $500.00 of price. The other is a Currituck land transfer tax, $1.00 for each $100.00 or fraction of price. The tax rates page repeats that second one in its Other Taxes list.

Under the statute the seller pays the excise tax at the counter ahead of recording. The county pages are silent on who carries the land transfer tax, so put that question to the office and to your closing attorney. Neither page gives a sample calculation, and the bill depends on your price, so get the amount in writing before closing.

sections.h2: Which fees does the Currituck County office charge for recording?
sections.html:
The county charges $26.00 for the first fifteen pages of a general instrument and $64.00 for the first thirty-five pages of a mortgage or deed of trust. Other charges on the fee page:

Charges printed on the Currituck fee page
ItemFee printed
Instruments in general, pages 1 to 15$26.00, then $4.00 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage, pages 1 to 35$64.00
Added instrument in one document$10.00
Satisfaction of deed of trust or mortgage$0.00 first reference, $25.00 for each added reference on the same instrument
Plats, maps and condominium unit ownership filings$21.00 each page
Certified copy of a document$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Uncertified copies at the office$.25 per page
Returned check$25.00

Copies sent through the mail run $1.00 a page. Mail requests also need a stamped return envelope.

sections.h2: How should a document be formatted for Currituck County recording?
sections.html:
A document that ignores the state's format rules (G.S. 161-14) is still recorded, but the office adds $25.00 for a non-standard document. The notices page spells out the rules:

  • Letter size (8 1/2 by 11) or legal size (8 1/2 by 14) paper.
  • Top margin of three inches on the opening page; half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black type or print on white paper, no smaller than 10 point.
  • Text on one side of each page only.
  • A title line naming the kind of instrument, placed first.

Blanks and corrections can be made in pen. Documents should also leave out Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, bank account numbers and similar identifiers unless the law requires them. Anyone can ask in writing that such numbers be removed from the online image of a record, and the county charges nothing for that request.

sections.h2: What is the farm proximity notice on Currituck County land records?
sections.html:
State law (G.S. 106-741) requires every county's land records to carry notice when a tract lies near a qualifying farm, which includes one within half a mile of a poultry, swine or dairy farm. Currituck keeps a file of parcels that may fall within half a mile of farm use property, and the posted file was last updated in February 2019.

For a seller with land away from the beach, the point is simple: buyers and their title searchers may see the notice. The statute says no cause of action arises just because a title searcher failed to report a farm nearby. If you are unsure whether your parcel is listed, ask the Register of Deeds staff to point you to the current file.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 Currituck County property tax rates?
sections.html:
The county-wide 2026 rate is .60 per $100 of valuation, down from .62 for 2025, and the county notes the rate is the same for land, buildings, mobile homes, boats, vehicles and business personal property. Several special districts add to it:

  • Carova Beach Road Service District: .02, shown as .62 combined.
  • Corolla Fire Protection Service District: .08, shown as .68 combined.
  • Knotts Island Fire Protection Service District: .09, shown as .69 combined.
  • Moyock Watershed Service District: .01, shown as .61 combined.
  • Ocean Sands North/Crown Point Stormwater: .255, with listed combinations for properties also in the water and sewer or fire districts.

The page also prints solid waste fees for 2026: $500.00 per dwelling unit on the southern Currituck beaches and $274.00 per dwelling unit on the mainland and northern beaches. A 6 percent occupancy tax is listed, which matters if the house has been a vacation rental. The county's tax office can tell you which districts cover your parcel.

sections.h2: How fast is Currituck County growing, according to the Census?
sections.html:
The 2020 count was 28,100 people; the mid-2025 estimate is 33,158, up 18.0 percent. Owners live in 87.3 percent of the occupied homes. Half of the owner-occupied homes are worth more than $378,800, by the Census median.

  • Land area: 261.91 square miles, or about 107 people per square mile.
  • Housing units: 18,351 (July 2025 estimate).
  • Median household income: $93,511 in 2024 dollars.
  • Residents 65 and over: 20.7 percent.
  • Average commute: 35.5 minutes each way.
  • New-construction permits in 2025: 325.

The office address is in the community of Currituck, and the Census table covers the whole county from Moyock to the northern beaches.

sections.h2: What should a Currituck County seller confirm before closing?
sections.html:
Confirm three things: the recorded owner, any deed of trust still open, and the special districts that tax the parcel. A search of the land records shows recorded deeds and deeds of trust, and a satisfaction recorded for a paid loan carries no fee for the first reference.

Next, have the closing attorney put both transfer taxes on the settlement statement, because the office collects them when the deed is presented. Ask the tax office for the balance on the current bill. Statewide, the due date is September 1 and interest begins January 6, so a fall or winter sale should settle whatever remains on the open bill. Sellers who are behind on a mortgage should know that foreclosure here follows the state's clerk-hearing process, with a ten-day upset bid period after the sale report.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Currituck Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The county footer shows weekdays from 8:00 AM until 5:00 PM, at 153 Courthouse Road. Holidays change the schedule, so confirm before driving over.

faqs.q: Does Currituck County charge a land transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. Besides the state excise stamp tax of $1.00 per $500.00, the county's pages show its own land transfer tax of $1 per $100 of price, counting any fraction.

faqs.q: How much is the Currituck County fee to record a deed of trust?
faqs.a: The county fee page prints $64.00 for a deed of trust or mortgage covering pages one through thirty-five. A satisfaction of a deed of trust is $0.00 for the first reference.

faqs.q: Can the Currituck Register of Deeds do a title search for me?
faqs.a: No. The office says it cannot provide legal advice, prepare documents or perform title searches. Staff explain how to look through the records on your own. A title search for a sale is the job of an attorney or title company.

faqs.q: What was the Currituck County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county-wide rate is .60 per $100 of valuation for 2026, with added rates in special districts such as Corolla Fire at .08 and Knotts Island Fire at .09. The county tax page prints the full schedule.
